meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty-five minutes, so let's start with why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
You asked for this meeting, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was anyone spoken to before it went in?
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
I'm writing down October 15, Hale. A student changing his argument between an outline and an essay isn't a finding, so which line is it? Show me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and no mark on his record.
What moved her: "Sorry. That came out wrong." gave you a little ground, enough that she stopped attacking and asked you a real question.
What cost ground: "I don't have time for this. The zero stands." put you back at the start, because it defended the zero before you had shown her anything.
Try next time: after you apologise, say plainly in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put the dated document in front of her before you describe it.
